title: Regional slowpath routing shim and caller-facing retry guidance for 5xx/timeouts
creator: Maya Singh
description: Summary: Several high-severity customer escalations over the past month have traced recurring 5xx/timeouts to regional frontdoor-to-runtime slowdowns and subsequent retry amplification. This ticket implements a regional 'slowpath' routing shim at the frontdoor and a short-term caller-facing retry guidance mechanism (SDK header + docs) to reduce customer-visible errors while we remediate root causes.
problem_statement: Under tenant surges or transient edge congestion, some requests hit a slow execution path (TLS handshakes/backpressure) that causes long tail timeouts. Clients retry aggressively (default SDK policies) producing amplified load and correlated 5xx waves across Hosted. Current mitigation (global rate-limiting and circuit breakers) reduces throughput but causes customer-visible failures and high-severity escalations.
proposed_solution: 1) Frontdoor slowpath routing shim: detect requests with elevated latency signals (conn attempts > threshold, partial responses, or upstream queued flag) and routable tenant header -> mark request 'slowpath'. Slowpath nodes run conservative configurations: extended per-request timeouts, serialized small batching, stricter per-tenant admission (burst token bucket), and faster KV-cache prefetches. 2) Caller-facing retry guidance: add new header X-RW-Retry-Hint to responses for slowpath/soft-fail cases with semantically parsed guidance (e.g., 'retry-after:2s,should-cap-retries'). 3) SDK update & docs: ship SDK minor release that recognizes X-RW-Retry-Hint and adjusts retry/backoff heuristics. 4) Telemetry and alerting: new Datadog metrics and SLO guardrails for slowpath ingress, and synthetic checks that emulate heavy-burst traffic.
acceptance_criteria:
- Slowpath flagging implemented and controlled via feature flag; ability to route to slowpath per-region.
- Canary in eu-west reduces 5xx spike rate for targeted tenants by >= 90% in observed incidents.
- X-RW-Retry-Hint header emitted for all slowpath responses and documented in SDK docs.
- SDK updated to respect header and reduces retry amplification in integration tests.
- Datadog dashboards display slowpath ingress, per-tenant admission drops, and recovery charts.
- Rollback plan: instant feature-flag off, traffic returns to normal routing within ~60s.
implementation_notes:
- Detection signals: edge connect time > 120ms, upstream queue depth > 50, partial streaming stalls.
- Slowpath nodes will use a conservative batch size=1..4 for generation ops and worker affinity to avoid KV thrash.
- Must ensure idempotency tokens are preserved across slowpath routing.
- Add API contract to docs for X-RW-Retry-Hint format (comma-separated key=val).
- Canary plan: 1) internal synthetic traffic for 24h, 2) 5% production traffic in eu-west for 2h, 3) 25% for 6h, 4) scale back or roll forward based on metrics.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: slowpath could increase latency for some tail requests; mitigate by strict canary + early kill-switch and telemetry.
- Risk: client SDK rollout mismatch leads to unchanged retry behavior; mitigate by conservative server-side admission for non-SDK clients (treat header as advisory but enforce server admission throttles).
- Risk: added complexity at frontdoor; mitigation: keep shrink-wrapped code, thorough unit tests, and runbook for SREs.
rollback_plan: Toggle feature-flag off at frontdoor to stop slowpath routing. Re-enable previous per-tenant circuit breakers and emergency admission policies. Notify customers about rollback via incident channel. Ensure telemetry captures revert window for postmortem.
